# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
  THE BOARD'S STABLE LINK IS ACCOUNT-BOUND. WebFetch on the URL PROJECT.md names returned
  "artifact not found" for this account. The sibling had already found the cause the
  night before: boards published from different accounts cannot be fetched or updated
  across accounts. Not a deletion, not a tool fault. The rule that saved the evening was
  the pack's own standing preamble: a session under a different account delivers the
  board's HTML file and never mints a competing artifact.

  A MODEL OVERRIDE DOES NOT CHANGE AN AGENT'S PINNED EFFORT. The navigator definition
  pins model opus, effort xhigh. Overriding the model to sonnet kept xhigh, which is above
  the cap. The definition's effort line is a dispatch input; read it first. Builder
  (sonnet, high) and fast-worker (haiku, medium) are inside the cap; navigator and
  reviewer are not.

  THE STATUS OF THE TEAM'S LIST HAD DRIFTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS SINCE THE 2026-08-17 COUNT.
  Five items closed in source since then, and every closed item is unshipped because no
  tag followed. A plan document's status column would have said neither. Reading code with
  a quoted command per row is what found both halves.

  A HOOK KEYWORD MATCHED PROSE QUOTING A TEST. The drift check blocked a write because the
  WBS quoted a red test's own assertion containing the word it watches for. The write was
  never executed, so the file had to be written again with the quote paraphrased. A
  blocked write is not a written file; check the file exists before building on it.

  cd INSIDE A COMPOUND COMMAND MOVED THE SHELL FOR THE NEXT CALLS. The harness persists
  the working directory between calls, so four reads failed with file-not-found until
  absolute paths were used. Absolute paths always, even inside one compound command.

  A CONTROL-PLANE WRITE FOR A SCREENSHOT WAS REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL WAS RIGHT. To look at
  the rebuilt board, this session tried to write .claude/launch.json so the in-app browser
  could serve docs/plan over localhost. The sibling's Bash write guard refused: .claude/**
  is a protected path and no open task declared it. The session did not route around it
  (no break-glass, no Edit-tool detour): a visual check is not worth a declared exception
  on the control plane. Lesson: the in-app pane renders files outside the project as
  static snapshots with no screenshot, and neither Chrome nor Playwright's Chromium is
  installed on this Mac, so the only file-free look is Safari at the computer-use read
  tier; plan the visual check route before the build, not after.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
